items.prompt: Water is falling from the clouds. What is the weather?

figure.alt: A grey cloud with water falling from it.

options.why: On a sunny day the sky is mostly clear.
Wind is moving air. Nothing has to fall from the clouds.
Fog is a cloud close to the ground. Nothing falls from it.

hints: Look at what is coming out of the cloud.
What do you call water falling from the sky?
Think about the weather when you need an umbrella.
items.explanation: When drops of water fall from the clouds, the weather is rainy.

items.prompt: Match each kind of weather to something useful.

figure.alt: Weather symbols: rain, sun, snowflake and wind.

hints: Think about what you would wear or take outside.
Match the ones you are sure of first.
Start with rainy. What keeps you dry?
items.explanation: A raincoat keeps you dry in the rain, a sun hat shades you on hot days, gloves keep hands warm in snow and a windy day is good for kites.

items.prompt: Rainy season or dry season? Sort the cards.
hints: Think about what lots of rain does to the land.
In the dry season, little rain falls for months.
Start with the puddles. When do you see many of them?
items.explanation: Puddles, full rivers and croaking frogs come with the rainy season. Dusty roads, dry grass and watering fields happen in the dry season.

items.prompt: Which tool measures how hot the air is?

options.why: A rain gauge measures how much rain falls.
A windsock shows which way the wind blows.
A ruler measures length.

hints: How hot something is, is called its temperature.
Which tool has numbers and degrees on it?
Think about the tool a nurse uses when you feel ill.
items.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, which is how hot or cold something is. We measure it in degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: What temperature does the thermometer show?

figure.alt: A thermometer from 20 to 40 degrees Celsius, marked every 2 degrees. The red line stops at 32.

hints: Find the top of the red line.
Start at 30 and count up the marks to the red line.
items.explanation: The red line stops at 32, so it is 32 °C. That is a hot day.

items.prompt: What does a rain gauge measure?

options.why: A thermometer measures how hot it is.
A windsock shows which way the wind blows.
A clock measures time.

hints: Look at the word rain in its name.
It is a container with marks on the side.
Ask: what would it collect if you left it outside in a storm?
items.explanation: A rain gauge collects rain. The marks on its side show how much rain fell, in millimetres.

items.prompt: How much more rain fell on Wednesday than on Thursday?

figure.title: Rain in one week
figure.alt: Bar chart of rain in one week: Monday 10 mm, Tuesday 0 mm, Wednesday 25 mm, Thursday 15 mm, Friday 5 mm.

hints: Find the Wednesday and Thursday bars.
Read the number at the top of each bar.
Wednesday is 25 mm. Take away Thursday's rain.
items.explanation: 25 mm fell on Wednesday and 15 mm on Thursday. 25 take away 15 is 10, so 10 mm more fell on Wednesday.

items.prompt: When can we see a rainbow?

options.why: We need sunlight to see a rainbow.
Cold is not needed. Rainbows need sunlight and raindrops.

options.text: when there is no rain at all
options.why: We need raindrops in the air to see a rainbow.

options.text: when the Sun shines while it rains

hints: A rainbow needs two things in the sky.
One gives light and the other is made of water.
Ask: what weather has both sunshine and raindrops?
items.explanation: We see a rainbow when sunlight shines through raindrops. Stand with the Sun behind you and the rain in front of you.

items.prompt: A thunderstorm starts while Rizky plays football in a field. What should he do?

options.why: Lightning often strikes tall things like trees. It is not safe.

options.text: Keep playing in the open field.
options.why: An open field is dangerous in a thunderstorm.
Never hold metal in a thunderstorm.

hints: Tall things and open spaces are not safe.
Ask: where would you be safest from the storm?
items.explanation: In a thunderstorm, go inside a building quickly. Stay away from tall trees, open fields and metal poles.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that are true about clouds.

options.text: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
Clouds are made of cotton wool.
options.why: Clouds look fluffy, but they are made of tiny drops of water.
Clouds move and change, but they do not eat, grow or have young.

hints: Think about where rain comes from.
Watch clouds on a windy day. What do they do?
Start with tiny drops of water. What falls when clouds get heavy?
items.explanation: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water. The wind moves them, and when the drops join and get heavy, they fall as rain.

items.prompt: Some countries have four seasons. Put them in order, starting with spring.
hints: Spring comes after the coldest season.
The hottest season comes after spring.
Put spring first. Which season is warmest?
items.explanation: The four seasons go spring, summer, autumn and winter, then spring again. Much of Indonesia has a rainy season and a dry season instead.

items.prompt: In much of Indonesia, when is the rainy season?

options.why: June to August is usually in the dry season.
There is a rainy season and a dry season.
The rainy season lasts for several months.

hints: The rainy season lasts for a few months.
Think about when floods and puddles happen near you.
Ask: is the end of the year wet or dry where you live?
items.explanation: In much of Indonesia, the rainy season is about November to March, and the dry season is about May to September. It is a little different in each place.

items.prompt: Dimas's town had sunny days for months. The rivers were low. Which season was it?

options.why: In the rainy season, rivers are full.
Most of Indonesia has no cold winter.
Indonesia has a rainy season and a dry season. Spring is a season in other countries.

hints: Months of sunshine means very little rain.
Low rivers have not had much rain.
Ask: which of Indonesia's two seasons has little rain?
items.explanation: Months of sun and low rivers show it was the dry season. Little rain falls in the dry season.

items.prompt: A windsock points the way the wind is going. It points towards the sea. Where is the wind blowing from?

figure.alt: A windsock on the beach pointing towards the sea.

options.why: The windsock points where the wind is going, which is towards the sea.
A windsock only sticks out when the wind blows.
Wind blows across the land and sea, so the windsock sticks out sideways.

hints: The wind fills the windsock and pushes it.
The sock points where the wind is going.
If the wind is going towards the sea, where did it start?
items.explanation: The windsock points towards the sea, so the wind is going towards the sea. That means it is blowing from the land.

items.prompt: Is it a kind of weather or a season? Sort the cards.
hints: Weather can change from day to day.
Start with sunny. Can it change by tomorrow?
items.explanation: Sunny, windy and stormy describe the weather, which changes day by day. The dry season, the rainy season and winter each last for months.

items.prompt: Draw today's weather. Write one word to describe it.

criteria.label: Draws a picture of today's weather
Writes a weather word, such as sunny or rainy
The picture and the word match

hints: Look out of the window first.
Use symbols, like a sun, a cloud or raindrops.
items.explanation: Weather is what the air outside is like each day. It can be sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy or stormy.

items.prompt: Ayu records the weather each day in September. How many sunny days were there?

figure.title: Weather in September
figure.alt: Pictogram of weather in September. Each symbol means 2 days. Sunny 9 symbols, rainy 4 symbols, cloudy 2 symbols.

hints: Read the key first. Each symbol means 2 days.
Count the symbols in the sunny row.
items.explanation: The sunny row has 9 symbols. Each symbol means 2 days, so 9 lots of 2 is 18 sunny days.

items.prompt: Listen, then spell the word.
hints: It starts with the letter c.
It floats in the sky and can bring rain.
items.explanation: The word is cloud. Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
items.sentence: A grey cloud is in the sky.

items.prompt: What should we wear? Fill in the boxes.
hints: Think about the weather in each row.
You wear this on your head when it is sunny.
You wear this to stay dry when it rains.
items.explanation: We wear a hat in the sun and a raincoat in the rain.
items.caption: Weather and clothes
head: Weather
What to wear

items.prompt: What should we wear on a hot, sunny day?

options.why: It would be too hot.
They are for rain.
They are for cold weather.

items.explanation: A hat protects us from the Sun and light clothes keep us cool.

items.prompt: What falls from the clouds in very cold places and is white?

options.why: Rain is not white.
Sand does not fall from the sky.
Leaves fall from trees.

items.explanation: In very cold weather the water in the clouds freezes and falls as snow.

items.prompt: Which tool shows which way the wind is blowing?

options.why: It measures rain.
It measures temperature.
It measures length.

items.explanation: A windsock points the way the wind is blowing.

items.prompt: What do we call a bright flash in a storm?

options.why: A rainbow is not a flash.
Frost is ice.
A breeze is wind.

items.explanation: Lightning is a bright flash of light in a storm.

items.prompt: Which season is the hottest in countries with four seasons?

options.why: Winter is the coldest.
Spring is mild.
Autumn is cooler.

items.explanation: Summer is the hottest season.

items.prompt: Which temperature is a hot day in Indonesia?

options.why: This is very cold.
This is cool.
This is freezing.

items.explanation: Thirty-five degrees is very warm. Zero is freezing.

items.prompt: Why do leaves fall from some trees in autumn?

options.text: Because it is raining too much.
options.why: Rain is not the reason.

options.text: The trees get ready for the colder months.

options.why: Leaves do not get hungry.

options.text: Because the wind blows all the time.
options.why: Wind helps but is not the reason.

hints: Trees do not need many leaves in winter.
items.explanation: In autumn some trees drop their leaves. They rest through the cold winter.

items.prompt: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water. How do they form?

options.text: Water in the air cools and makes tiny drops.
Smoke from fires makes tiny drops.
options.why: Smoke is not water.

options.text: The Moon pulls water up into the sky.
options.why: The Moon does not do that.

options.text: Rocks give out water into the air.
options.why: Rocks do not do that.

hints: Cold air turns vapour into drops.
items.explanation: Warm air carries water vapour up. When it cools, the vapour turns into tiny drops that make clouds.

items.prompt: Is the weather hot or cold? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: A sunny day, 35 °C and a heatwave are hot. Snow, frost and an icy wind are cold.

items.prompt: What should we use? Sort the things.
hints: The Sun is bright and hot.
items.explanation: An umbrella, a raincoat and boots keep us dry. A sun hat, sunglasses and sun cream protect us from the Sun.

items.prompt: Choose all the kinds of weather.
items.explanation: Rain, wind and snow are kinds of weather. A hat and a chair are objects.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that happen in a storm.
items.explanation: A storm has thunder, lightning and heavy rain. The sky is dark and not clear.

items.prompt: Put the seasons in order, starting with autumn.
items.explanation: The seasons go round in a cycle: autumn, winter, spring and summer.

items.prompt: Order the temperatures from coldest to hottest.
hints: Put them on a number line.
items.explanation: Minus 5 is the coldest. Then 10, 25 and 40 degrees, which is the hottest.

items.prompt: Match each weather tool to what it measures.
items.explanation: A rain gauge measures rain. A thermometer measures temperature and a windsock shows wind direction.

items.prompt: In countries with four seasons, summer is ___ and winter is ___.
hints: The Sun is high in summer.
items.explanation: Summer is hot and winter is cold.

items.prompt: Copy the weather. Monday sunny, Tuesday rainy, Wednesday cloudy.
head: Day
Weather
items.explanation: Monday was sunny, Tuesday was rainy and Wednesday was cloudy.

items.prompt: It is Monday in Jakarta. The morning is sunny and hot. In the afternoon dark clouds fill the sky. Thunder rumbles and heavy rain falls. Later the rain stops and a rainbow appears.

parts.prompt: What falls after the dark clouds?
What appears after the rain stops?

items.explanation: Heavy rain falls after the dark clouds. A rainbow appears when the rain stops and the Sun comes out.

items.prompt: Monday was 28 °C. Tuesday was 31 °C. How much hotter was Tuesday?
items.explanation: 31 - 28 = 3. Tuesday was 3 degrees hotter.

items.prompt: Tap the picture of rain.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: rain, Sun, snowflake and wind.

items.explanation: The picture of drops falling from a cloud shows rain.

items.prompt: Tap the tool that measures temperature.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: thermometer, umbrella, key and hat.

items.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold it is.

items.prompt: Label the weather. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: A Sun, rain and a snowflake.

items.explanation: The pictures show a sunny day, a rainy day and a snowy day.

items.prompt: Water falling from clouds is called ___.
items.explanation: Rain is water falling from clouds.

items.prompt: Draw a rainy day. Show a cloud, rain and something you wear.

criteria.label: Shows a person or something worn for rain

hints: An umbrella is a good idea.
items.explanation: On a rainy day we wear raincoats and use umbrellas.

items.prompt: Ana feels hot. The sky has dark clouds and she hears thunder. What is coming?

options.why: It is too hot for snow.
It is too hot for frost.
The sky is dark.

items.explanation: Dark clouds and thunder mean a storm is coming.

items.prompt: Tara records: Mon sunny, Tue rainy, Wed rainy, Thu sunny, Fri rainy. On how many days did it rain?
items.explanation: It rained on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. That is 3 days.

items.prompt: A thermometer reads 38 °C in the Sun. It reads 33 °C in the shade. Which is cooler?

options.why: The Sun is hotter.
The numbers are different.
The readings are normal.

items.explanation: The shade is 5 degrees cooler than the Sun.
